scope: Extra public open practice for previously underserved routes

items.prompt: A laptop has original price \(\pounds 100\). Its price increases by \(10\%\), then the new price is reduced by \(10\%\). Find the final price in pounds and explain why the changes must be applied successively.

mark_scheme.text: Explain that each percentage is of the new price.

items.prompt: A community group shares \(\pounds 20\) between Projects A and B in the ratio \(2:3\). Calculate both shares. A volunteer claims that each project receives the same amount; explain briefly why this is not correct.

mark_scheme.text: Explain the parts differ, so the allocations differ.

items.prompt: A rectangular garden is \(5\text{ m}\) long and \(3\text{ m}\) wide. Fencing costs \(\pounds 4\) per metre. Calculate the perimeter and total fencing cost. Explain why calculating the area would not give the amount of fencing needed.

mark_scheme.text: Fencing follows the boundary length rather than covering the area.

items.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled independently and their results are added. Calculate the probability that the sum is exactly \(6\). Explain why the sample space contains \(36\) ordered outcomes.

mark_scheme.text: List or count 5 ordered pairs summing to 6.
There are 6 × 6 equally likely ordered pairs.
Explain that order matters: (a,b) and (b,a) are separate when a differs from b.

items.prompt: Two alarm lights flash together at noon. One flashes every 6 minutes and the other every 8 minutes. After how many minutes do they next flash together, and at what clock time will that occur? Show your method.

mark_scheme.text: Find multiples or prime factors of both periods.
Use the LCM as the next simultaneous event.
State \(24\text{ minutes after noon}\) (and corresponding clock time).

items.prompt: A bicycle costs \(\pounds 120\) before a price increase of \(10\%\). Find the amount of the increase and the new price. Explain which quantity the percentage is taken from.

mark_scheme.text: The percentage is of the original price.

items.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides of lengths \(6\text{ cm}\) and \(10\text{ cm}\), and perpendicular height \(4\text{ cm}\). Calculate its area and include the correct units.
Five assessment scores are 4, 5, 6, 7 and \(k\). Their mean is \(6.8\). Calculate \(k\), clearly showing the total score required.

mark_scheme.text: Find the sum \(22\) of known scores.

items.prompt: A straight ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is \(3\text{ m}\) from the wall, and its top touches the wall \(4\text{ m}\) above the ground. Assuming the wall and ground form a right angle, calculate the ladder length. State the geometrical principle used.

mark_scheme.text: Recognise the ladder is the hypotenuse.

mark_scheme.text: A ticket cannot be bought as a fractional item in this context.

mark_scheme.text: Replacement keeps the total and composition unchanged.
